correctness.rationale: The exact rank-one q and rho inputs were independently read from their original mathematical full texts, including normalizations and parameter domains. For \(q<1\) the derivative sign of the positive ratio equals \(G(c)=\eta-q+s(\eta+c)/\sqrt{1-c^2}\), with G strictly increasing and \(G(0)=\eta(1+s)-q\), giving unique minima and endpoint maxima. The stated critical overlap and squared-root identities simplify exactly with \(q^2+s^2=1\), yielding the closed-form minimum; both endpoint constants and max ties follow by direct comparison. \(q=1\) is a separate monotone or constant rational case. Each overlap is realized by an explicit nonzero rank-one operator in any dimension at least two; the proof is not a finite computational extrapolation. A standard-library exact rational verifier checks independent examples and degeneracies.

value.rationale: A motivated natural complete classification of sharp comparison factors between two independently used numerical-radius gauges on all nonzero rank-one Hilbert operators. The exact minimizer shifts sharply from genuinely oblique rank-one geometry to nilpotent orthogonality at \(\eta=q/(1+\sqrt{1-q^2})\); the maximizer has a separate orthogonal-to-parallel transition. The constants support optimal transfer of inequalities for rank-one operators and cannot be inferred from a pointwise fixed-operator bound without optimizing the full geometry. The result does not claim a new individual-radius formula or general higher-rank transfer.
